answers.brief_reasoning: substring(begin, end) throws an exception if begin < 0, if end > length, or if begin > end. Here begin = start and end = start + len, so the method is safe exactly when start ≥ 0, len ≥ 0, and start + len ≤ s.length(). That is option D. Option B is too strict because it rules out start + len == s.length(), which is valid. Option C is too strict because it rules out len == 0, which is also valid. Option A does not guarantee safety, since start could be negative.
